findings.description: A long-lived AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in cleartext as Lambda environment variables in the Terraform source. Anyone with repository access, Terraform state access, or lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration can retrieve and reuse these credentials.

No kms_key_arn is set, so environment variables containing secrets are protected only by the default AWS-managed key and are displayed in plaintext through the console/API to any principal with function read permissions. A customer-managed CMK with a restricted key policy would add an access-control boundary around these secrets.
The function runs on nodejs12.x, which is past end of support and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the execution environment unpatched.

No vpc_config block is defined, so the function executes outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or network segmentation controls, providing an unmonitored exfiltration path if the function or its dependencies are compromised.

The assume-role policy grants sts:AssumeRole to the lambda.amazonaws.com service principal with no aws:SourceAccount or aws:SourceArn condition, so the trust is not scoped to a specific account or function, weakening the trust boundary against confused-deputy abuse.
